subproblem.title: Finitely many n-covectors separate n-vectors
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ there are N ∈ ℕ and n-covectors b₁, …, b_N on ℝ^P (elements of Covector (Eucl P) n, the continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ) such that every n-vector w (an element of NVector (Eucl P) n, i.e. a continuous linear functional on n-covectors) with w(b_i) = 0 for all i is the zero functional.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ (N : ℕ) (b : Fin N → Covector (Eucl P) n), ∀ w : NVector (Eucl P) n, (∀ i, w (b i) = 0) → w = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. Covector (Eucl P) n = (ℝ^P)[⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ is the space of continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ; its addition and scalar multiplication are pointwise. NVector (Eucl P) n = Covector (Eucl P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ is the space of continuous linear functionals on covectors. Let e₁, …, e_P be the standard basis of ℝ^P (Mathlib `(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis`). This is the basis argument of step 7 of the parent proof; finite-dimensionality of the space of covectors is proved here because it is not an available instance in the frozen import closure.

1. (Evaluation on basis tuples.) Define Φ : Covector (Eucl P) n → ℝ^(Fin n → Fin P) by Φ(α)(r) := α(e_{r(1)}, …, e_{r(n)}) for r : Fin n → Fin P. Since (α + β)(v) = α(v) + β(v) and (c·α)(v) = c·α(v) for all tuples v, Φ is ℝ-linear (both identities hold by definition).

2. (Φ is injective.) Suppose Φ(α) = Φ(β). Then the underlying multilinear maps of α and β (`α.toContinuousMultilinearMap.toMultilinearMap`) agree on every tuple (e_{r(1)}, …, e_{r(n)}) of basis vectors. A multilinear map on a finite family of modules with bases is determined by its values on tuples of basis vectors: writing v_i = Σ_k v_i(k)·e_k and expanding by multilinearity, α(v₁, …, v_n) = Σ_{r : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_i v_i(r(i)))·α(e_{r(1)}, …, e_{r(n)}), and likewise for β (Mathlib `Module.Basis.ext_multilinear`). Hence α(v) = β(v) for every v ∈ (ℝ^P)ⁿ, so α = β.

3. (The covectors form a finite-dimensional space.) ℝ^(Fin n → Fin P) is a finite-dimensional real vector space (a finite product of copies of ℝ) and Φ is an injective linear map into it, so Covector (Eucl P) n is finite-dimensional (Mathlib `FiniteDimensional.of_injective`). (Mathlib's instance `Module.Finite.multilinearMap` would also yield this, but its module is not imported by `GMT.Ch06.Submission`; the injection Φ avoids it.) Let N := dim_ℝ Covector (Eucl P) n and let b₁, …, b_N be a basis of Covector (Eucl P) n (Mathlib `Module.finBasis`).

4. (Separation.) Let w be an n-vector with w(b_i) = 0 for every i. Every covector α can be written α = Σ_i c_i·b_i with real c_i, so by linearity of w, w(α) = Σ_i c_i·w(b_i) = 0. (Equivalently, the linear maps w and 0 agree on a basis and are therefore equal, Mathlib `Basis.ext`.) Hence w(α) = 0 for every covector α, i.e. w = 0 as a continuous linear map. ∎

Formalization aid (not part of the mathematical argument). The following Lean proof of exactly this frozen statement compiled (Lean v4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c, frozen project d8d46c9, shared pinned packages) when placed inside `namespace Submission` immediately before `theorem main_theorem` in a scratch copy of GMT/Ch06/Submission.lean; `#print axioms` gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], and the comparator's generated NodeSolution module (`exact Submission.lpf_rsn_covector_separating_family`) typechecks:

```lean
theorem lpf_rsn_covector_separating_family : ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ (N : ℕ) (b : Fin N → Covector (Eucl P) n), ∀ w : NVector (Eucl P) n, (∀ i, w (b i) = 0) → w = 0 := by
  intro P n
  let e : Module.Basis (Fin P) ℝ (Eucl P) := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis
  let Φ : Covector (Eucl P) n →ₗ[ℝ] ((Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ) :=
    { toFun := fun α r => α (fun i => e (r i))
      map_add' := fun _ _ => rfl
      map_smul' := fun _ _ => rfl }
  have hΦ : Function.Injective Φ := by
    intro α β h
    have hm : α.toContinuousMultilinearMap.toMultilinearMap =
        β.toContinuousMultilinearMap.toMultilinearMap :=
      Module.Basis.ext_multilinear (fun _ => e) (fun r => congrFun h r)
    ext v
    exact congrArg (fun m : MultilinearMap ℝ (fun _ : Fin n => Eucl P) ℝ => m v) hm
  haveI : FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Eucl P) n) := FiniteDimensional.of_injective Φ hΦ
  let b := Module.finBasis ℝ (Covector (Eucl P) n)
  refine ⟨Module.finrank ℝ (Covector (Eucl P) n), b, ?_⟩
  intro w hw
  have hlin : (w : Covector (Eucl P) n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) = 0 := b.ext (fun i => by simpa using hw i)
  ext α
  simpa using congrArg (fun l : Covector (Eucl P) n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ => l α) hlin
```
proof_key_steps: Φ(α)(r) := α(e_{r(1)}, …, e_{r(n)}) is a linear map from covectors to the finite-dimensional space ℝ^(Fin n → Fin P).
Φ is injective because a multilinear map is determined by its values on tuples of basis vectors (Module.Basis.ext_multilinear).
Hence Covector (Eucl P) n is finite-dimensional (FiniteDimensional.of_injective); take a basis b₁, …, b_N (Module.finBasis).
A linear functional vanishing on a basis is zero.

audit.reason: The exact finite-separation statement follows from the injective evaluation map on basis tuples, finite-dimensionality and basis extensionality. The supplied proof covers degenerate dimensions and requires neither the parent nor another child.

subproblem.title: Null on every vanishing relatively compact open set implies null off the support
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current T ∈ D_n(U) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), every set M ⊆ ℝ^P with M ⊆ U and every measure μ on ℝ^P: if μ(M ∩ W) = 0 for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P such that closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U and T vanishes on W (T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W), then μ(M ∖ spt T) = 0. Here spt T = T.support = U ∖ Z_T, where the zero region Z_T = T.zeroRegion is the union of all such sets W.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)), M ⊆ U → (∀ W : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen W → IsCompact (closure W) → closure W ⊆ U → T.VanishesOn W → μ (M ∩ W) = 0) → μ (M \ T.support) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). μ is an arbitrary measure on ℝ^P; it is applied to arbitrary sets as an outer measure, and only monotonicity and countable subadditivity are used. For the current T ∈ D_n(U) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), "T vanishes on W" (`T.VanishesOn W`) means T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) (`TestFormOn U n`) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Let 𝒮 be the family of all W ⊆ ℝ^P such that W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U and T vanishes on W. By definition (SimonGMT `GeometricCurrentOn.zeroRegion`, `GeometricCurrentOn.support`; Simon Ch. 6, 2.11) the zero region is Z_T := T.zeroRegion = ⋃₀ 𝒮 and spt T := T.support = U ∖ Z_T. This is steps 1, 2 and 9 of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary measure.

1. (M ∖ spt T ⊆ Z_T.) Let x ∈ M with x ∉ spt T. Since M ⊆ U, x ∈ U. If x ∉ Z_T, then x ∈ U ∖ Z_T = spt T, contradicting x ∉ spt T. Hence x ∈ Z_T.

2. (A countable subfamily has the same union.) Every member of 𝒮 is open and ℝ^P is second countable. Hence there is a countable subfamily 𝒮′ ⊆ 𝒮 with ⋃₀ 𝒮′ = ⋃₀ 𝒮 = Z_T (Lindelöf property of second-countable spaces; Mathlib `TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable`).

3. (Covering.) Let x ∈ M ∖ spt T. By steps 1 and 2, x ∈ Z_T = ⋃₀ 𝒮′, so x ∈ W for some W ∈ 𝒮′; since also x ∈ M, x ∈ W ∩ M. Hence M ∖ spt T ⊆ ⋃_{W ∈ 𝒮′} (W ∩ M).

4. (Every piece is null.) Let W ∈ 𝒮′. Then W ∈ 𝒮, so W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U and T vanishes on W. The hypothesis gives μ(M ∩ W) = 0, i.e. μ(W ∩ M) = 0.

5. (Conclusion.) Since 𝒮′ is countable, countable subadditivity and step 4 give μ(⋃_{W ∈ 𝒮′} (W ∩ M)) ≤ Σ_{W ∈ 𝒮′} μ(W ∩ M) = 0 (Mathlib `measure_biUnion_null_iff`). By step 3 and monotonicity (`measure_mono_null`), μ(M ∖ spt T) = 0. ∎

Formalization aid (not part of the mathematical argument). The following Lean proof of exactly this frozen statement compiled (Lean v4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c, frozen project d8d46c9, shared pinned packages) when placed inside `namespace Submission` immediately before `theorem main_theorem` in a scratch copy of GMT/Ch06/Submission.lean; `#print axioms` gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], and the comparator's generated NodeSolution module (`exact Submission.lpf_rsn_null_diff_support_of_local_null`) typechecks:

```lean
theorem lpf_rsn_null_diff_support_of_local_null : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)), M ⊆ U → (∀ W : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen W → IsCompact (closure W) → closure W ⊆ U → T.VanishesOn W → μ (M ∩ W) = 0) → μ (M \ T.support) = 0 := by
  intro P n U T M μ hMU hloc
  obtain ⟨S', hS'c, hS'S, hS'eq⟩ := TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable
    {W : Set (Eucl P) | IsOpen W ∧ IsCompact (closure W) ∧ closure W ⊆ U ∧ T.VanishesOn W}
    (fun W hW => hW.1)
  have hsub : M \ T.support ⊆ ⋃ W ∈ S', W ∩ M := by
    intro x ⟨hxM, hxs⟩
    have hxZ : x ∈ T.zeroRegion := by
      by_contra hx
      exact hxs ⟨hMU hxM, hx⟩
    have hxZ' : x ∈ ⋃₀ S' := by
      rw [hS'eq]; exact hxZ
    obtain ⟨W, hW, hxW⟩ := hxZ'
    exact Set.mem_biUnion hW ⟨hxW, hxM⟩
  refine measure_mono_null hsub ?_
  rw [measure_biUnion_null_iff hS'c]
  intro W hW
  obtain ⟨hWo, hWc, hWU, hWv⟩ := hS'S hW
  rw [Set.inter_comm]
  exact hloc W hWo hWc hWU hWv
```
proof_key_steps: Since M ⊆ U, M ∖ spt T ⊆ Z_T = ⋃₀ 𝒮, where 𝒮 is the family of open W with compact closure inside U on which T vanishes.
Lindelöf (second countability of ℝ^P): a countable subfamily 𝒮′ ⊆ 𝒮 has the same union (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable).
Hence M ∖ spt T ⊆ ⋃_{W ∈ 𝒮′} (W ∩ M), and μ(M ∩ W) = 0 for each W ∈ 𝒮′ by hypothesis.
Countable subadditivity and monotonicity give μ(M ∖ spt T) = 0.

audit.reason: Prose and Lean type match exactly. M ⊆ U gives the zero-region inclusion; a countable open subcover, nullity of each intersection and measure monotonicity prove the conclusion. No measurability assumption or circular dependency is hidden.

subproblem.title: Fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations with a positive weight on a set
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, M, W ⊆ ℝ^P with W open and M μ-null-measurable, θ, g : ℝ^P → ℝ and C ∈ ℝ. Assume (i) θ(x) > 0 for every x ∈ M; (ii) θ is μ-integrable on M ∩ W; (iii) g is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞M = μ.restrict M; (iv) |g(x)| ≤ C for μ⌞M-a.e. x; (v) ∫_M θ(x)·(φ(x)·g(x)) dμ(x) = 0 for every C^∞ function φ : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ W. Then for μ⌞M-a.e. x, x ∈ W implies g(x) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (M W : Set (Eucl P)) (θ g : Eucl P → ℝ) (C : ℝ), IsOpen W → NullMeasurableSet M μ → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ W) μ → AEStronglyMeasurable g (μ.restrict M) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict M), |g x| ≤ C) → (∀ φ : Eucl P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ W → ∫ x in M, θ x * (φ x * g x) ∂μ = 0) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict M), x ∈ W → g x = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P carries its Borel σ-algebra; μ⌞M := μ.restrict M, and ∫_M h dμ is by definition ∫ h d(μ⌞M). "C^∞" means `ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)`. This is steps 4–7 of the parent proof with the positive weight moved from the measure ν = θ·μ⌞(M ∩ W) into the integrand: we apply the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations to f := θ·g and the measure μ⌞M, and divide by θ at the end. (In the parent's notation, θ·g = 0 μ⌞M-a.e. on W is the same as g = 0 ν-a.e., and ν-null and μ-null subsets of M ∩ W coincide because θ > 0 on M.)

1. (f := θ·g is integrable on W for μ⌞M.) W is open, hence Borel, so (μ⌞M)⌞W = μ⌞(W ∩ M) = μ⌞(M ∩ W) (Mathlib `Measure.restrict_restrict`). By (ii), θ is integrable for μ⌞(M ∩ W). subproblem.title: A unit-oriented rectifiable representation has null carrier where the current vanishes
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U, W ⊆ ℝ^P with W open and W ⊆ U. Let T ∈ D_n(U) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) vanish on W (T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W). Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Hⁿ-null-measurable (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), θ : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ > 0 on M and θ Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ W, and ξ : ℝ^P → NVector (Eucl P) n a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M with ‖ξ(x)‖ = 1 (operator norm) for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x. If T(ω) = τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U), then Hⁿ(M ∩ W) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → T.VanishesOn W → NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ W) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ ((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M) → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ‖ξ x‖ = 1) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = tauAction n M θ ξ ω) → (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) (M ∩ W) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. μ := Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P = Eucl P and μ⌞M := μ.restrict M. n-covectors α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n carry the multilinear operator norm and n-vectors w ∈ NVector (Eucl P) n = Covector (Eucl P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ the operator norm, so |w(α)| ≤ ‖w‖·‖α‖ (`ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm`). Dⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n consists of the C^∞ maps ω : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) n with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U (`IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ U`, where `IsTestForm ω = IsSmoothForm ω ∧ HasCompactSupport ω`), and tauAction n M θ ξ ω = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x). This is steps 5–8 of the parent proof for one fixed open set W; the analytic step 6 is the sibling weighted_fundamental_lemma and the basis argument of step 7 is the sibling covector_separating_family.

1. (Coordinate functions.) Fix an n-covector α and put g_α(x) := ξ(x)(α). Evaluation at α, w ↦ w(α), is a continuous linear map NVector (Eucl P) n → ℝ (`ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ α`); composing it with the μ⌞M-a.e.-strongly measurable map ξ shows that g_α is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞M. For μ⌞M-a.e. x we have ‖ξ(x)‖ = 1 and hence |g_α(x)| ≤ ‖ξ(x)‖·‖α‖ = ‖α‖.

2. (Testing T with φ·α.) Let φ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ W, and put ω(x) := φ(x)·α. Then ω is C^∞ (a smooth scalar function times a constant covector; `ContDiff.smul` with `contDiff_const`), ω has compact support (`HasCompactSupport.smul_right`), and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ W ⊆ U (`tsupport_smul_subset_left`). So ω ∈ Dⁿ(U). Because tsupport ω ⊆ W and T vanishes on W, T(ω) = 0. By the representation hypothesis and the linearity of ξ(x), ξ(x)(φ(x)·α) = φ(x)·ξ(x)(α), so
   0 = T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(φ(x)·α) dμ(x) = ∫_M θ(x)·(φ(x)·g_α(x)) dμ(x).

3. (Each coordinate vanishes a.e. on M ∩ W.) Apply the sibling lemma weighted_fundamental_lemma with the measure μ, the sets M and W, the weight θ, the function g := g_α and the constant C := ‖α‖. Its hypotheses hold: W is open; M is μ-null-measurable; θ > 0 on M; θ is μ-integrable on M ∩ W; g_α is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞M and |g_α| ≤ ‖α‖ μ⌞M-a.e. (step 1); and the test integrals vanish (step 2). Hence for μ⌞M-a.e. x: x ∈ W ⇒ ξ(x)(α) = 0.

4. (ξ vanishes a.e. on M ∩ W.) By the sibling lemma covector_separating_family there are N ∈ ℕ and covectors b₁, …, b_N such that an n-vector vanishing on every b_i is zero. Apply step 3 with α = b_i for each of the finitely many i and intersect the resulting full-measure sets (`ae_all_iff`): for μ⌞M-a.e. x, for all i, x ∈ W ⇒ ξ(x)(b_i) = 0. For such x with x ∈ W, the n-vector ξ(x) vanishes on every b_i, so ξ(x) = 0.

5. (Contradiction with the unit norm.) Intersect further with the full-measure set where ‖ξ(x)‖ = 1. If such an x lay in W, step 4 would give ξ(x) = 0 and hence ‖ξ(x)‖ = ‖0‖ = 0 ≠ 1 (`ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_zero`). Hence for μ⌞M-a.e. x, x ∉ W, i.e. (μ⌞M)(W) = 0 (`ae_iff`). Since W is open, hence Borel, (μ⌞M)(W) = μ(W ∩ M) (`Measure.restrict_apply`), so μ(M ∩ W) = 0. ∎

In the frozen scope the norm on NVector (Eucl P) n is `ContinuousLinearMap.hasOpNorm`; the generic lemmas `norm_zero`, `norm_neg` and `norm_nonneg` may fail to rewrite against it, whereas `ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_zero`, `ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_neg`, `ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_nonneg` and `ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm` apply directly.

```lean
theorem lpf_rsn_local_null : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → T.VanishesOn W → NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ W) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ ((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M) → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ‖ξ x‖ = 1) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = tauAction n M θ ξ ω) → (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) (M ∩ W) = 0 := by
  intro P n U W T M θ ξ hW hWU hvan hM hpos hθ hξm hξ1 hrep
  have key : ∀ α : Covector (Eucl P) n,
      ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), x ∈ W → ξ x α = 0 := by
    intro α
    refine lpf_rsn_weighted_fundamental_lemma P (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) M W θ
      (fun x => ξ x α) ‖α‖ hW hM hpos hθ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · exact (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ α).continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable hξm
    · filter_upwards [hξ1] with x hx
      calc |ξ x α| = ‖ξ x α‖ := (Real.norm_eq_abs _).symm
        _ ≤ ‖ξ x‖ * ‖α‖ := (ξ x).le_opNorm α
        _ = ‖α‖ := by rw [hx, one_mul]
    · intro φ hφ hφc hφW
      let ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n := fun x => φ x • α
      have hωs : IsSmoothForm ω := hφ.smul contDiff_const
      have hωc : HasCompactSupport ω := hφc.smul_right
      have hωW : tsupport ω ⊆ W := (tsupport_smul_subset_left φ (fun _ => α)).trans hφW
      let ωU : TestFormOn U n := ⟨ω, ⟨hωs, hωc⟩, hωW.trans hWU⟩
      have h0 : T ωU = 0 := hvan ωU hωW
      rw [hrep ωU] at h0
      simpa [tauAction, ωU, ω, map_smul, smul_eq_mul] using h0
  obtain ⟨N, b, hb⟩ := lpf_rsn_covector_separating_family P n
  have hall : ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ∀ i, x ∈ W → ξ x (b i) = 0 :=
    ae_all_iff.mpr (fun i => key (b i))
  have hnotW : ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), x ∉ W := by
    filter_upwards [hall, hξ1] with x hx h1 hxW
    have h0 : ξ x = 0 := hb (ξ x) (fun i => hx i hxW)
    rw [h0, ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_zero] at h1
    exact zero_ne_one h1
  have hres : (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M W = 0 := by
    rw [ae_iff] at hnotW
    simpa using hnotW
  rw [Measure.restrict_apply hW.measurableSet, Set.inter_comm] at hres
  exact hres
```
proof_key_steps: For each covector α, g_α = ξ(·)(α) is μ⌞M-a.e.-strongly measurable and |g_α| ≤ ‖α‖ μ⌞M-a.e. (unit norm).
Testing T with ω = φ·α (φ ∈ C_c^∞, tsupport φ ⊆ W) gives ∫_M θ·(φ·g_α) dHⁿ = 0, because T vanishes on W.
weighted_fundamental_lemma: ξ(x)(α) = 0 for μ⌞M-a.e. x ∈ W.
covector_separating_family plus a finite intersection of full-measure sets: ξ(x) = 0 for μ⌞M-a.e. x ∈ W.

The two declared dependencies give ξ = 0 almost everywhere on W, contradicting unit norm and yielding the exact measure-zero conclusion. The proof is complete and non-circular.
